record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and linked PUBLISHABLE_RESULTS.md were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports outcomes of a weight-editing refusal-removal method on multiple models, testing the practical weight-edit claim. Its custom benign-subspace-preserving LoRA edits are not the original activation-projection intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports matched benchmark results for ICONOCLAST and a HERETIC-style baseline. The README describes candidate direction estimators, but does not report results isolating any particular estimator or testing the original projection at every layer and position. Setup instructions and test commands are not result evidence.
record.test_reason: The README reports harmful-request refusal counts after a weight edit on 10 open-weight models, which bears on V2. The edit is a LoRA rank-one or low-rank change built from refusal directions projected out of a benign PCA subspace and tuned by Optuna. That is a different weight-edit recipe aimed at the same practical-removal question. There is no unedited-model refusal baseline. HERETIC is a comparator method, not a control.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim ICONOCLAST wins 10/10 matched comparisons under a lexicographic selection rule: refusals, then overrefusals, then KL. It has strictly fewer harmful refusals in 6/10 and lower KL in 8/10. Benign-subspace preservation is presented as removing refusal without a utility cost. Of the 10 wins, 4 are refusal ties decided on overrefusals, and Falcon's win comes with much higher KL (6.14).
record.recipe_differences: A related directional-abliteration weight-edit approach, but it projects candidate directions out of a harmless-activation subspace and applies rank-one or low-rank LoRA edits with multi-objective selection; it is not the original per-layer, per-position activation projection. Tool/research repo with benchmark results reported in the README.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported refusal outcomes vary across the ten model conditions; Falcon3-7B-Instruct has a much higher ICONOCLAST KL value than HERETIC (6.1448 vs. 0.1648).

fits_no_version.finding: Benign overrefusal counts on 64 Alpaca holdouts after the edit, compared with the HERETIC baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign-subspace-preserving abliteration yields no more benign overrefusals than standard directional abliteration.

fits_no_version.finding: First-token KL from the unedited model is lower than HERETIC in 8 of 10 models. It is higher for Falcon3-7B (6.14 vs 0.16) and Yi-1.5-9B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projecting refusal directions out of a benign subspace reduces the distribution drift caused by abliteration, though not in every model.

record.problems: Repository code and linked detailed results were not read or run. The README reports a matched benchmark and comparator but no unedited-model refusal baseline, uncertainty estimates, or direct general-capability evaluation; KL and benign overrefusal are not general capability measures.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. The file list includes other reports and result files, but their contents are not available in the supplied text and were not treated as reported results.

untested.parts: Pure difference-in-means activation ablation at all layers and positions; inducing refusal by adding the direction; general capability benchmarks.
Refusal rates of the unedited models; general capability (e.g. MMLU) after the edit; prompt sets beyond 20 JailbreakBench holdouts; reasoning or larger models.
Not tested. Low-rank edits are an option, but no results separate rank-one from multi-direction edits.

missing.what: Unedited-model harmful refusal counts on the same 20 holdouts, needed to measure how much refusal the edit removed
Detailed per-model results and any capability evaluations for the ICONOCLAST edits

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is a README table only, with no uncertainty and n=20 harmful prompts. The edit's hyperparameters are tuned by Optuna on refusal and KL objectives, and the reported prompts are called holdouts. Whether they were used in the search itself is unclear. The repo's earlier experiments (pipelines/, results/) concern PII unlearning via abliteration, not refusal. The README contained no instructions to follow.

versions.untested_parts: No direct test of the original difference-in-means direction with activation ablation at every layer and position, addition-induced harmless refusals, or general capability preservation.

The README does not report results against unedited versions of the models; the reported comparison is against HERETIC-style edits. It does not establish how the edits perform beyond the stated benchmarks.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test comparing affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from refusal decisions.
No reported transfer test across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No test of how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
No reported test in reasoning models.
